html:
Kuringgai, also spelled Guringai or Ku-ring-gai, is a name used for the Aboriginal Australian people of the coast north of Sydney Harbour, around Broken Bay and Pittwater. Some writers stretch it to all the speakers of the Gathang language as far north as Port Macquarie.

The name comes from the writer John Fraser, who coined it in 1892, and many historians doubt it was a real people's name. The clans of this coast are also counted among the Dharug or linked with the Awabakal and Darkinjung to the north.

The clans of Broken Bay met the First Fleet settlers from 1788, and the smallpox epidemic of 1789 killed a large share of them. Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park, set up in 1894, carries the name today.
